problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
H=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 3 & 0\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}],\,K=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $A$, we have

$$
\det({A})=1 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 1 = 0.
$$

Because $\det(A)=0,$ we conclude that $A$ is not invertible. Since $A$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $A$ is singular.

- The matrix $B$ is a $3 \times 2$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
\det({C})=3 \cdot 3 - (-3) \cdot 3 = 18.
$$

Because $\det(C) \neq 0,$ we conclude that $C$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $A$ is singular.

feedback.worked_solution:
Given a $2\times 2$ matrix

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}a & b \\ c & d\end{aligned}],
$$

the inverse of $B$ can be found using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(B)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

First, we compute the determinant:

$$
det(B)=2\cdot 0-1\cdot 1=-1
$$

Using the formula, then, the inverse is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(B)}[\begin{aligned}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{(-1)}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can verify the result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}B{B}^{-1} & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓ \\ {B}^{-1}B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
